source:
Create a AAA-quality endless runner for Roblox inspired by the fast-paced gameplay of classic endless runners like Temple Run 2. The experience should capture the same adrenaline, fluid movement, exploration, and progression while using entirely original characters, environments, animations, music, sounds, UI, and level assets.
The game should feel polished enough to compete with top Roblox experiences.
Core Gameplay
Create an endless runner where the player automatically runs forward.
The player can:
 • Swipe Left → Turn Left
 • Swipe Right → Turn Right
 • Swipe Up → Jump
 • Swipe Down → Slide
 • Collect coins
 • Dodge obstacles
 • Navigate branching paths
 • Achieve high scores
 • Complete missions
 • Unlock cosmetics and characters
Movement should be smooth and highly responsive.

Motion Controls
On supported mobile devices, add optional motion controls using the device's accelerometer and gyroscope.
Features:
 • Tilt left/right to steer or subtly change lane position
 • Optional head-look camera effect
 • Motion sensitivity slider
 • Calibration screen
 • Toggle motion controls on/off
 • Automatic fallback to swipe controls if motion sensors are unavailable
 • Low-latency filtering to reduce jitter
 • Dead zones and smoothing for comfortable play
Motion controls should enhance gameplay without replacing core swipe controls.

Endless World Generation
Implement procedural generation that creates an endless path while maintaining handcrafted quality.
Include diverse original environments such as:
 • Ancient jungle ruins
 • Mountain temples
 • Lava caverns
 • Ice canyons
 • Desert ruins
 • Floating islands
 • Bamboo forests
 • Waterfalls
 • Forgotten cities
 • Underground caverns
Generation should avoid impossible obstacle combinations and maintain fair difficulty.

Obstacles
Create a large variety of original obstacles:
 • Gaps
 • Broken bridges
 • Fallen trees
 • Rolling boulders
 • Rotating blades
 • Swinging axes
 • Spike traps
 • Crumbling floors
 • Fire traps
 • Moving platforms
 • Collapsing bridges
 • Narrow ledges
 • Climbing sections
 • Rope swings
 • Zip lines
Difficulty should scale naturally as the run progresses.

Collectibles
Implement:
 • Coins
 • Rare gems
 • Power crystals
 • Treasure chests
 • Mystery relics
 • Keys
 • Daily collectibles
 • Seasonal collectibles

Power-ups
Create an extensible power-up system including:
 • Coin magnet
 • Temporary shield
 • Speed burst
 • Double coins
 • Slow-motion
 • Invincibility
 • Extra life
 • Auto-collect
 • Lucky treasure boost
Each should include:
 • Visual effects
 • Audio feedback
 • UI timers
 • Upgrade paths

Enemy Chase
Create an original pursuing creature that keeps pressure on the player.
Features:
 • Dynamic catch-up system
 • Difficulty scaling
 • Different chase phases
 • Escape mechanics
 • Cinematic introductions
 • Intelligent obstacle interaction

Missions
Implement hundreds of procedurally generated missions such as:
 • Collect coins
 • Travel distance
 • Jump count
 • Slide count
 • Near misses
 • Perfect turns
 • Consecutive runs
 • Power-up usage
 • Treasure collection

Progression
Create long-term progression:
 • Character unlocks
 • Outfit customization
 • Cosmetic trails
 • Pets
 • Skill upgrades
 • Permanent upgrades
 • Daily rewards
 • Weekly events
 • Achievements
 • Prestige system

Graphics
Create high-quality original visuals featuring:
 • Dynamic lighting
 • Volumetric fog
 • Weather
 • Water effects
 • Particle systems
 • Animated foliage
 • Day/night cycle
 • Cinematic camera
 • Smooth animations
 • Optimized performance across devices

Audio
Compose completely original music inspired by adventurous orchestral and tribal themes.
Include:
 • Ambient exploration music
 • Chase music
 • Menu music
 • Victory sounds
 • Coin collection
 • Power-ups
 • Environmental ambience
Do not use copyrighted music.

Roblox Features
Integrate:
 • DataStore
 • ProfileService
 • Leaderboards
 • Badges
 • Daily rewards
 • Cloud saves
 • Cross-device support
 • Mobile optimization
 • Console support
 • PC support

Performance
Optimize for:
 • 60+ FPS on modern devices
 • Graceful quality scaling
 • Streaming Enabled compatibility
 • Efficient procedural generation
 • Object pooling
 • Minimal memory usage

Code Architecture
Use clean, modular Luau code with separate systems for:
 • Runner Controller
 • Input Manager
 • Motion Control Manager
 • Procedural Generation
 • Obstacle Manager
 • Collectible Manager
 • Mission System
 • Progression System
 • Save Manager
 • UI Framework
 • Audio Manager
 • Camera Controller

QA & Polish
Do not stop after the first playable version.
Continue iterating by:
 • Automatically testing every gameplay mechanic
 • Verifying procedural generation never creates impossible paths
 • Stress-testing long runs
 • Testing all motion controls across supported devices
 • Optimizing performance
 • Eliminating bugs
 • Refining animations, controls, camera, and game feel
Repeat testing and refinement until the experience is polished, performant, and feels like a premium endless runner with original content suitable for Roblox.

answers.ask: How long should one generated stretch be before the biome changes?
answers.answer: Use short, readable biome stretches of roughly 60–90 seconds of running before transitioning to the next environment, with a brief blended transition segment.

answers.ask: How often should the path fork, and do the forks rejoin or commit the player to a branch?
answers.answer: Present a fork about every 20–30 seconds on average, and have branches rejoin after a short alternate segment so runs remain procedurally manageable and fair.

scene_prompt: Create a 3D endless-runner map with a forward-running path that procedurally passes through original adventure environments: ancient jungle ruins, mountain temples, lava and underground caverns, ice canyons, desert ruins, floating islands, bamboo forests, waterfalls, and forgotten cities. Build each biome as a short, readable 60–90-second stretch, joined by brief blended transition segments. Arrange a clear central route with collectible trails and varied traversable hazards including gaps, broken or collapsing bridges, fallen trees, rolling boulders, rotating blades, swinging axes, spike and fire traps, crumbling floors, moving platforms, narrow ledges, climbing sections, rope swings, and zip lines. About every 20–30 seconds, split the route into branching paths that rejoin after short alternate segments. Use dramatic terrain, animated foliage, water, weather, fog, dynamic lighting, and day-to-night atmosphere, with a pursuing original creature visible behind the runner during chase sections.
blob:
### Genre
The dominant genre is Infinite Runner: automatic forward motion, reactive dodging, and an endless procedurally assembled route define the experience.

### Shape and preset
Use `lane-free`, a Free Lateral Steering route that lets the runner steer around hazards and choose short forks rather than snap between fixed lanes. This matches the Chase Runner preset, extended with the prompt’s collectible and biome-generation requirements.

### Config requirements
Visible geometry: `chunk-modular` builds seamless authored-looking biome chunks with aligned entry and exit pivots; `hazard-kill` supplies gaps, traps, fire, collapsing spans, and fall-away edges; `obstacle-jump` supplies bridges, logs, ledges, climbing sections, rope swings, and zip lines; `obstacle-moving` supplies boulders, blades, axes, moving platforms, and collapsing elements; `barrier-horizon` uses fog, turns, canyon walls, and dense foliage to conceal incoming chunks. `water-body` provides waterfalls, rivers, and cavern water; `terrain-relief` provides temples, canyons, cliffs, and volcanic ground; `island-cluster` provides the floating-island biome. Invisible layout: `collectible-nodes` places pickup volumes in readable trails along safe and risky lines.

### Layout components
Build an endless central forward route from modular chunks. Each biome occupies a readable 60–90-second stretch, followed by a brief blended transition chunk: ancient jungle ruins, mountain temples, lava and underground caverns, ice canyons, desert ruins, floating islands, bamboo forests, waterfalls, and forgotten cities. About every 20–30 seconds, split the main route into two short alternate branches that visibly rejoin at a common continuation chunk. Keep every branch legible, with hazards arranged as avoidable obstacle sequences rather than clutter. Place collectible trails through central safe lines and toward riskier side routes. Use stone ruins, broken and collapsing bridges, fallen trees, trap assemblies, narrow ledges, rope rigging, zip lines, animated foliage, waterfalls, weather effects, fog, and a pursuing original creature visible behind the runner during chase sections. Bound each chunk with cliffs, canyon walls, dense vegetation, cavern walls, water, or void edges. Frame the isometric view down the forward route, with approaching hazards and the next focal biome transition readable ahead.

### Render order
Use `topdown`: the generated route, forks, rejoins, and obstacle-clearance topology must remain valid for play, while this is not a carveable maze or racing circuit eligible for `authored_plan`.

### Scale, theme, and pipeline cost
Scale is huge, driven by an endless modular route spanning nine distinct biome families. Theme is AAA adventurous fantasy expedition, cinematic and perilous, with lush natural contrast, elemental caverns, and ancient architecture. Pipeline modifiers: `P6` because each emitted chunk sequence, fork, rejoin, and hazard gap must be valid by construction; `CHECK` because waterfalls, water crossings, floating islands, rope swings, and zip lines introduce localized open-volume traversal that must not self-occlude. Terrain elevation is tiered without requiring a separate pass, so no additional modifier is forced.

options.text: Seamless authored-looking biome chunks with aligned entry and exit pivots build the endless central forward route.
Gaps, traps, fire, collapsing spans, and fall-away edges form avoidable obstacle sequences.
Bridges, logs, ledges, climbing sections, rope swings, and zip lines provide traversable hazards.
Boulders, blades, axes, moving platforms, and collapsing elements animate the route.
Fog, turns, canyon walls, and dense foliage conceal incoming chunks.
Waterfalls, rivers, and cavern water appear across the biome route.
Temples, canyons, cliffs, and volcanic ground provide dramatic tiered terrain.
A floating-island biome forms part of the procedural expedition.
Pickup volumes form readable collectible trails along central safe lines and riskier side routes.
